what-changed-on-main-since-the-first-pla.text: What changed on main since the first plan.
Read on 38c7fbc1; every item below was checked against the tree, not recalled.

strategy.text: The model leads. The registry library gets one pure function for the window and one for the within-batch rule, named as the model names them, so the selection, the builder and the command line call the same thing instead of three copies of a comparison. The conformance unit suite asks the model the same question through the driver transport and requires equal verdicts at the boundary and one past it. The validator is not edited; its refusals are pinned by tests, by contexts evaluated against its compiled bytes, and by one live row.

four-pull-requests.text: Each ships a runnable outcome and carries the pages for what it ships. One patch per slice in a patch stack, no journey commits. Every pull request is cut from the merge of the one before it. The cut is by the fan-out of a Lean change: a Lean change fans out to dozens of files, mostly regenerated or restamped, each rule needs its own pass, and one pull request for both would be a working day of consumer repair. Pull requests 1 and 2 are the model's, in the order the constitution requires; pull requests 3 and 4 depend on the model and on nothing of each other.

the-lean-pull-requests-stay-two-and-why.text: The Lean pull requests stay two, and why.
The desk asked on 2026-10-14 whether pull requests 1 and 2 stay two or become one. They stay two.

Each one can be stopped. A Lean change fans out to the same consumers every time: five corpora regenerated in two passes, the simulator's mirror, the coverage record and its fixed counts, the theorem register, the readme counts, the open-datum application's proofs, the narration. One pull request would carry both rules' model work, driver rows and consumer repair in one writer run of at least 5 hours of writer time, which is the first overrun trigger before the first push, and nothing would land if it overran. Two pull requests have the triggers 5 and 6.5 hours, and the first lands alone.

The first lands early. Pull request 1 is the smaller one (3 to 3.5 hours). The one row it changes in the permanent contract's corpus is already ruled (the desk answered A by the operator's ruling of 2026-10-06 on #396; the pull request body names the corrected row and that ruling). The protected rejection lane (#494) rewrites the fold model in its later slices and rebases onto this ticket's Lean changes; two small rebases onto the same two match arms cost less than one large one.
What one pull request would save is the second consumer pass, about 1.5 to 2 hours of writer time and one hosted run of 60 to 90 minutes. That does not outweigh an early, stoppable first landing.
Pull requests 1 to 3 are on the Demo 1 path, because pull request 3 states the builder's refusals in the words of both model rules; pull request 4 is evidence and is not.

pull-request-1-the-model-refuses-what-a-.text: Pull request 1: the model refuses what a batch creates and consumes.

Runnable outcome: anyone can ask the model's driver the batch question for an insertion then a termination of one key (the conformance transport's batch question, replayed by nix run .#conformance-appendix-tests from conformance/, and the row in lean/driver-corpus.json) and read token-missing, where the model accepted the pair before; the permanent contract's accepted batch is now a batch on two distinct keys. No runtime behavior changes.

batch-statements-first. The statements, stated and committed failing: the pair refused; a termination of a pre-existing holding accepted; an accepted batch burning only live holdings; independent requests folding as a batch.

created-holdings-in-foldBatch. The list of keys the batch has created so far, the refusal token-missing after the mint check (the validator's order), the proofs repaired (foldBatch_inv, fold_batch_cons, the batch-of-one statement), the permanent contract's anchor reselected.

consumers-follow-the-batch-rule. The driver and permanent-contract rows for every same-key pair, the regenerated corpora in two passes (the statement digests written into the scenario sources must equal the exported manifest), the simulator's mirror, rules and gate, the coverage record and its fixed counts, the open-datum application's proofs, docs/theorems.md, the README counts, the narration clips whose text changes, and the first constitution amendment.

Estimate, commit-owner time: 3 to 3.5 hours (the Lean sources and proofs about 1 hour with lake build as the inner loop; the rows and the two-pass export about 45 minutes; the simulator and the coverage record about 45 minutes; the application proofs, the register and the constitution about 45 minutes), then 60 to 90 minutes of hosted CI. Overrun trigger: 5 hours.

pull-request-2-the-model-admits-a-fold-o.text: Pull request 2: the model admits a fold only inside its window.

Runnable outcome: anyone can ask the model's driver the fold question under a validity upper bound one past a request's deadline and read not-phase1, and at the deadline read it admitted (same command and corpus), where the model admitted both before; a reject is admitted in any window and a retraction is unchanged.

admission-statements-first. The statements, stated and committed failing: the boundary, any expired request, each request by its own submission time, admission before the law, a reject reading no time.

fold-admission-in-the-model. Request.submittedAt, the fold witness, the admission, the fold arm of the exit admission, the batch under a witness, the adjusted permanent-contract statements (excluded_fold and its neighbours), proofs.

driver-and-corpora-under-a-witness. Every fold scenario and fold batch carries a witness; a fold without one is unsupported; rows for the boundary, an expired request, a batch in and past its window; the regenerated corpora in two passes.

transport-live-driver-simulator. The conformance transport and the live driver read the request's submission time off its datum and the upper bound off the built transaction; the simulator's schema, actions, rules, gate and playable fold; the mirror.

register-book-constitution. The coverage record and counts, the register, the README counts, the conformance book sentence that called the window a tracked discrepancy, the second constitution amendment, narration.

Estimate, commit-owner time: 4 to 4.5 hours (the Lean sources and proofs about 1 hour; the driver, rows and two-pass export about 1 hour; the transport and the live driver about 1 hour; the simulator about 45 minutes; the register, book and constitution about 45 minutes), then 60 to 90 minutes of hosted CI including every live conformance job. Overrun trigger: 6.5 hours. The harvested branch is the guide: its model slice is about 130 lines of Lean source and 170 of statements, and its consumers about 25 files.

pull-request-3-the-builder-enforces-it-a.text: Pull request 3: the builder enforces it and the receipt names it.

Runnable outcome: singular registry fold with an expired and an in-window request pending settles the in-window one and prints the expired one not-phase1 as a model refusal, where it printed window-closed as processor policy; a fold the builder would sign outside a window or with a termination of a key its own batch inserts is refused before signing.

admission-in-the-library. The new pure module with the two functions, their unit tests and the conformance agreement test with its failing control (a version that admits one past the deadline must fail it).

builder-refuses-before-signing. The builder entry points call the library after building, reading the bound from the built body; the within-batch refusal carries the model's reason; both name the request.

selection-and-receipt-in-the-models-words. The selection's window rule (judgeAlone in FoldSelection.hs) calls the library at the probe bound, and ReasonWindowClosed becomes the model refusal not-phase1; window-closed is deleted in the same change from every reader the table above lists (FoldSelection.hs, CLI/Fold.hs, CLI/FoldRules.hs, their three specs, the Demo 1 journey script and docs/singular-node.md); the command line's post-build decision calls the library; the receipt names the request, the reason, the source, the deadline and the probe bound. A deadline equal to the probe bound, which window-closed refused, is now admitted, as the model and the chain admit it; the receipt pages and the pull request body state that change.

devnet-expired-request-named-by-the-model. #518's own devnet item already leaves an expired request pending beside a fresh in-window one and asserts the excluded entry's reason and source (fold_selection_excluded in tools/demo1_cli_journey.sh, line 1926: window-closed, selection-policy). This slice re-points that one assertion to not-phase1 and model-refusal, keeps its failing control, and adds no second devnet item: the settled in-window request and the named expired one are one run.
docs-of-what-ships. The pages that describe the fold, the two vocabularies and the residuals; speech re-stamped; narration regenerated.

Estimate, commit-owner time: 3 to 3.5 hours (the library module and the agreement test about 1 hour; the builder and the selection about 1 hour; the receipt, the readers and the scripts about 1 hour; the pages about 30 minutes), then 60 to 90 minutes of hosted CI including the Demo 1 jobs. Overrun trigger: 5 hours.

pull-request-4-the-compiled-validator-is.text: Pull request 4: the compiled validator is shown to refuse the mutated transaction.

Runnable outcome: nix flake check in onchain/ turns red when the validator's window rule moves by one millisecond or its burn discharge is removed, and one dedicated conformance row compares the chain's refusal with the model's not-phase1.

validator-window-and-same-key-tests. Aiken tests for the exact boundary under the ledger's excluded upper bound, for different submission times, for an open bound, for an expired reject beside an in-window update, for reason precedence, and for the four same-key pairs, each with its accepted twin and each asserting the traced reason.

compiled-contexts-and-fault-control. The same transactions exported as labelled contexts; the boundary checker evaluates them against the blueprint's compiled state bytes; its always-accept fault control must fail on the new labels; the label counts are derived from the discovered set.

live-fold-window-row. One dedicated conformance row on a devnet: a registry of its own, a fold built with an upper bound past one request's deadline, refused by the ledger, answered not-phase1 by the model, attributed by script hash. It runs inside the existing batch job so that no required check is added. It is the last slice and the only one nothing else in the pull request depends on: if the suite's own mechanism (the published evidence page and its receipts) makes it larger than the budget, it is cut at its checkpoint and filed as a follow-up, and the pull request ships without it.
book-and-docs. The conformance book and the pages follow; speech and narration.

Estimate, commit-owner time: 2.5 to 3 hours (the Aiken tests about 1 hour; the exported contexts and checker rows about 1 hour; the live row about 1 hour), then 60 to 90 minutes of hosted CI. Overrun trigger: 4.5 hours. The pull request edits test files of the validator surface only; the table below says what happens if another lane has moved them.

script-identity-no-pull-request-of-this-.text: Script identity: no pull request of this ticket moves it.

The desk expected the on-chain change to move the script identities (onchain/script-identity.json, onchain/permanent-contract.json, the registry pin cascade) and asked which pull request does. None does, because no validator source is edited. The evidence, on 38c7fbc1:

Pull request 4 adds Aiken test files and edits the fixtures module onchain/lib/registry_fixtures.ak, which only tests import (the registry's tests and the open-datum application's open_datum.tests.ak, so its new parameters carry defaults) and which lies outside the documentation guard's extent of state.ak and lib/registry/. The checks script-identity, blueprint, aiken-suite and the application's application-script-identity and application-aiken-suite prove the hashes unchanged, and the path fence in the gate proves no validator source changed. The registry pin and the permanent-contract file therefore do not move in this ticket. Two other lanes plan validator edits that do move them, and they are not this ticket's: #495 (the expiry clock and the finite-interval reader in shared.ak, fold.ak and request.ak) and #529 (the request tag). One consequence stays visible: the model, the builder and the chain say one thing about the window only while the chain keeps this window predicate; if #495 changes in_phase1, pull request 4's tests move with it. The schedule for a fresh preprod registry follows whichever pull requests the desk lands, not this ticket.

team-process-and-merge-order.text: Staffing (operator rulings for this lane, 2026-10-14, from the desk's release note): Lean model work is written by Codex gpt-6-astra at high effort (codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -C <worktree> -m gpt-6-astra -c model_reasoning_effort=high), which makes pull requests 1 and 2 its work; implementation code by Muse (/home/paolino/.local/bin/muse --approve), which makes pull requests 3 and 4 its work; the auditor is Grok (grok --always-approve -m grok-4.7 --effort high) in a read-only audit worktree, persistent, mute toward the writer, an alarm that blocks only with a concrete failure scenario; the ticket owner stays Claude Sonnet 5.5 at xhigh effort. One writer at a time in the lane. No draft tool and no other seat. These rulings bind this lane only. Codex drops the first pointer after a fresh start, so no writer is relied on before its pane-bound START is in its journal. The gate was written by the ticket owner and a second seat independently and synthesized once (the second author was the GLM seat of the planning run, retired).

Plan review. The first plan was reviewed on 2026-10-09 against the seven planning-quality lines, with amendments all applied here. This re-derived plan and the touch-list question that names it go to the desk; no writer starts before the answer is on disk.

Dispatch. One commit owner per pull request, each with the whole pull request as its task and the terminal condition green, blocked or at capacity; no run counting, no nudges. The auditor is launched beside it from the first run and is mute toward it. Checkpoints: the failing statements or tests of each slice, each acceptance line green, and before the push. The push waits for every checkpoint to be approved. Pull request 1 is dispatched first. Pull request 2 is a new dispatch after pull request 1 merges, pull request 3 after pull request 2, and pull request 4 after pull request 2 and in the writer's turn after pull request 3.

Gate budget. Existing commands only. The local candidate gate carries a budget of 40 minutes per candidate and runs what the slice can break; the repository aggregate runs once on the final candidate; hosted CI is the net. Local runs respect the 50 MiB receipt cap of #513; no hosted job is rerun locally. Every new test is deterministic: pure functions with fixed times, no wall clock, no timing margin; the one test that waits on a deadline is the existing devnet item.

Lean changes. Before the first push of pull requests 1 and 2 the commit owner runs every consumer the touch list names for it: the model job, the simulator and browser checks, the coverage commands, the conformance unit suite. A Lean change fans out to consumers no single gate enumerates; the list is there so that none is found one hosted run at a time.

Merge order. Pull requests 1 and 2 first, ahead of the other Lean lanes (desk, 2026-10-14); then in the desk's order and one slot at a time; no rebase, retarget or merge without a granted slot. When every checkpoint is approved and the exact head is green, the ticket owner asks for the slot and merges with a merge commit once it is granted and the rebased head is green again.
The touch list binds. A file that is not on it and that the work later needs is a question to the epic owner, forwarded to the desk, before it is edited.

Commits. No attribution trailer of any kind; the commit range is searched for one before the push. Spec and plan commits stay local; the first push is the reviewed candidate, as a draft pull request, because every push to the pull request starts the whole hosted matrix.

evidence-this-ticket-produces.text: Receipts: the failing and passing runs of each slice's focused check; the conformance unit run with its failing control; the compiled-context evaluation with the always-accept fault control failing; the hosted run links for the executed items (an in-window request admitted and an expired one left out and named on a devnet; the live window row) and for every required check at the exact head. The pull request body is a fill-in of the repository template:

Left uncovered, written before the work: the model's batch transaction; equal root bytes for two orders of independent requests; the batch's leaves, holdings, mint and payments equal to those of each request folded alone; an open validity bound in the model; the retraction witness's duplicate submission time; the ledger's own refusal reason, which the deployed validators do not trace; prose of the pages.

budget-and-size.text: One team per epic at a time; the operator is on credits. The split is decided above, before dispatch, with an estimate per pull request: 3 to 3.5 hours, 4 to 4.5 hours, 3 to 3.5 hours and 2.5 to 3 hours of commit-owner time, each followed by 60 to 90 minutes of hosted CI that the merge waits for. A pull request that passes its overrun trigger without every checkpoint approved is stopped at its last green checkpoint and the remainder is proposed to the epic owner as a question, not ground out.
